sections.label: CEA complaints and improvement areas
sections.summary: Complaints against estate agents fell 34% from 2011 to 2019, but three areas need improvement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Almost 10 years on, the number of complaints against estate agents and salespersons received by CEA has dropped by 34%, from 1,170 complaints in 2011 to 777 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The number of concluded cases involving misrepresentation of property-related information to clients has declined by 98%, from 404 cases to 2011 to 10 cases just in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: And the number of concluded cases involving dual representation, which is a serious offence, has seen a 97% decline, from 59 cases in 2011 to two cases in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: While the number of complaints has gone down, there remains scope for improvement in three areas: first, to strengthen Singapore’s levers against money laundering and terrorism financing in the real estate agency industry; second, to strengthen CEA’s disciplinary levers to better deter and punish errant estate agents and salespersons; and last, but not least, to enhance CEA’s investigative powers to better enable CEA to identify and take action against errant estate agents and salespersons.

sections.label: FATF money laundering compliance
sections.summary: Clause 8 introduces a new Part IVA in the Estate Agents Act to comply with FATF Recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: On this basis, setting out the duties to counter potential money laundering and terrorism financing in CEA’s practice guidelines does not meet FATF’s standards for preventive measures, as the duties and penalties must be spelt out expressly in the Estate Agents Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Hence, to comply with FATF Recommendations, clause 8 will introduce a new Part IVA in the Estate Agents Act on the prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing.

sections.label: CEA censure and financial penalty
sections.summary: Clauses 6 and 11 let CEA censure errant estate agents and salespersons and impose a $5,000 maximum penalty per case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clauses 6 and 11 amend sections 36 and 49 of the Act respectively, to allow CEA to censure errant estate agents and salespersons, and publish the censure on the public register.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: It also allows CEA to impose a maximum financial penalty of $5,000 per case.

sections.label: Higher Disciplinary Committee penalties
sections.summary: Clause 13 raises maximum financial penalties to $200,000 for estate agents and $100,000 for salespersons, up from $75,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: In addition, to better deter serious breaches, clause 13 of the Bill will amend section 52 to increase the maximum financial penalty the Disciplinary Committee can impose to $200,000 per case for estate agents, and $100,000 per case for salespersons, up from $75,000 today.

sections.label: Salesperson penalty matches commissions
sections.summary: The new $100,000 maximum penalty for salespersons better matches their commissions, which are generally lower than estate agents'.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Similarly for salespersons, the new maximum financial penalty of $100,000 per case will better match the commissions received by salespersons, which are generally lower than that of estate agents, but can also be quite high.

sections.label: Continued action and transaction records
sections.summary: Clauses 5 and 16 allow investigations and disciplinary action to continue after licences or registrations are not renewed, and clause 7 requires transaction records.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To prevent such estate agents and salespersons from trying to evade punishment by leaving the industry, clauses 5 and 16 complement the amendments by making clear that, after disciplinary proceedings have commenced, even if the estate agent’s licence or salesperson’s registration are not renewed, investigations may continue and disciplinary action can still be taken against them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Bill will also make other changes to improve and clarify the regulatory framework and to facilitate CEA’s operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: It makes clear that CEA can collect and publish transaction records of estate agents and salespersons on the public register, to help consumers make more informed decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 7 inserts a new section 43A, which requires estate agents and salespersons to submit transactions records to CEA, and provides that non-compliance without reasonable excuse or the submission of false information knowingly is an offence.

sections.label: CPD courses and Disciplinary Panel size
sections.summary: CPD courses are a licence renewal requirement, and Clause 12 lets CEA set the Disciplinary Panel size beyond 20.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: CPD courses are a renewal requirement for licences and registrations, to ensure that estate agents and salespersons possess the necessary knowledge to provide professional service to their clients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Lastly, Clause 12 will amend section 51(1) to allow CEA to determine the size of the Disciplinary Panel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This provides CEA the flexibility to increase the size of the Panel beyond the current limit of 20, should the caseload increase in future.

sections.label: Respondents' views on changes
sections.summary: Estate agents, salespersons and industry associations were supportive or neutral to the changes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The respondents, comprising estate agents, salespersons and industry associations, were supportive or were neutral to the changes.

sections.label: Rising numbers in recent years
sections.summary: Numbers have been going up again, reaching 894 in 2018, the highest in six years since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But in recent years, the numbers have been going up again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It was 894 in 2018, highest in six years since 2013.

sections.label: Property agent fined and suspended
sections.summary: A property agent was fined $30,000 and suspended 12 months for offers made without his client's knowledge, causing a loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A recent high-profile case last year saw a property agent fined $30,000 and suspended for 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: He had made offers to a seller of a condominium unit without his client’s knowledge, with the purpose of negotiating a higher commission for himself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This resulted in the client making a final offer which was higher than necessary and suffering a loss of between $20,000 and $30,000.

sections.label: AML/CFT standards for real estate
sections.summary: The regulations aim for international standards, raising questions on AML/CFT standards, agency understanding of risks and compliance culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that on this matter, the regulations aim to have the real estate industry comply with international standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But would these be the same standards as those imposed on the financial services sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, just like for the financial sector, AML/CFT, which takes a preventive approach that combines tough licencing and comprehensive reporting requirements, strict AML/CFT regulations and risk-based supervision of the relevant financial and non-financial sectors, what is the extent at which these agencies understand the AML/TF risks and how it can be enhanced?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Most importantly, how can we promote a culture of compliance within the real estate agencies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singapore's property market plays a crucial role in driving our economy and nation building.

sections.label: Improving professional standards of property agents
sections.summary: Professional standards of property agents and estate agents have improved, and the Government constantly reviews them to move with the times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Over the years, professional standards of property agents and estate agents have improved and I am glad that the Government is constantly reviewing these standards to ensure that it moves with the times.

sections.label: Higher maximum financial penalties
sections.summary: The speaker supports raising the CEA Disciplinary Committee's maximum financial penalty to $200,000 for licensed estate agents and $100,000 for registered salespersons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With over 90% of our population homeowners, many will rely heavily on property agents for their property transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support the proposed increase in the maximum financial penalty that the Council of Estate Agencies (CEA) Disciplinary Committee can impose, from the current $75,000 to $200,000 for licensed estate agents and $100,000 for registered salespersons.

sections.label: Complaints against property agents
sections.summary: The speaker asks for an update on 2019 complaints against property agents, CEA sanctions, and consideration of a demerit points system for minor breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Could the Minister of State provide an update on the nature and the number of complaints against property agents in 2019 and how many agents have been sanctioned by the CEA as a result?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For minor disciplinary breaches, I would like to ask if the Ministry could consider a demerit points system, so that first-time minor breaches by property agents, especially those who are new to the industry, such as advertising-related breaches, would not result in a Letter of Censure or a financial penalty.

sections.label: Customer due diligence duties
sections.summary: The Bill provides for customer due diligence checks, record-keeping of checks and documents, and submitting Suspicious Transaction Reports under the CDSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The Bill provides for duties to conduct customer due diligence checks, to keep records of the checks and relevant documents and to also submit Suspicious Transaction Reports, as required under the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act or CDSA.

sections.label: Censure and financial penalties
sections.summary: For less serious disciplinary breaches, amended section 49 lets CEA censure errant estate agents and salespersons and impose financial penalties of up to $5,000 per matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For disciplinary breaches that are not as serious, the new powers under section 49, as amended by clause 11, allow CEA to censure errant estate agents and salespersons and impose financial penalties of up to $5,000 per matter.

sections.label: CEA complaints in 2019
sections.summary: The speaker states that CEA received 777 complaints in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In my opening speech, I mentioned that CEA received 777 complaints in 2019.

sections.label: Annual CPD training requirement
sections.summary: Each salesperson must complete about six to nine hours of CPD training annually to renew his registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Each salesperson must complete about six to nine hours of CPD training annually in order to renew his registration.

sections.label: CEA estate agency support measures
sections.summary: CEA started a SkillsFuture Study Award in 2018 for salespersons' upskilling, and is studying a suggestion to waive licence and registration renewal fees amid COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: CEA started the SkillsFuture Study Award for the estate agency industry in 2018 to support salespersons in upskilling and acquiring skillsets and competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Lastly, Mr Melvin Yong suggested that CEA waive the licence and registration renewal fees for estate agents and salespersons in view of the COVID-19 situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We have received a few similar requests from the industry recently and, rest assured, we are studying the matter carefully.
